newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht hits 13-yearr high offshore.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht hits 13-yearr high offshore.

text.p: The Thai baht shot to its highest level against the dollar for 13 years on Thursday as offshore players scrambled for baht to cut their positions amid a severe shortage of funds.
The baht jumped to 23.900/24.000 to the dollar offshore from 24.360/24.410 late on Wednesday. It was the highest level for the currency since Thailand's baht devaluation in 1984.
In Bangkok, the baht was much softer at 25.835/25.840, near the Bank of Thailand (BOT)'s midrate of 25.82.

A two-tier offshore and onshore baht market has been in place since mid-May after speculative attacks on the currency prompted the BOT to impose what dealers called capital controls to cut off baht supply to offshore speculators.
"A lot of maturities are coming up so people have no choice but to cut their positions. It's very expensive to roll over to the longer maturities," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.

As the offshore scramble for baht raged, the central bank denied market talk that it would buy dollars in offshore markets at 24.00 baht to help bail out speculators caught short of baht. "We have no interest whatsoever to buy dollars in the offshore market," a senior BOT official told Reuters.
Dealers said the denial was aimed at hitting back at speculators who held positions against the baht.

A European bank dealer in Singapore said there was limited scope for the baht to strengthen further. "It makes no sense below 24.00 (to the dollar). I think we won't see the baht much lower than 23.50/24.00," he said.
There was no consensus over how long the BOT's controls might stay in place with dealers and economists expecting a period of anywhere between two weeks and six months.
They all agreed, however, that a lifting of the controls without an accompanying change in Thailand's foreign exchange regime would spur another speculative attack.

"Given the BOT's foreign reserves, this thing can't drag on for more than three to five months. It's really just a question of who will give up first: the speculators or the BOT," the U.S. bank dealer said.
In Indonesia, the funding shortage in the baht caused longer-term forwards to rise on fears of a similar squeeze.
"Our forward market is a bit in disorder because of the Thai factor. Offshore players fear a similar move in Jakarta despite a denial by Bank Indonesia," a dealer in Jakarta said.
She said offshore players were going long in forwards to factor in possible risks although they had to pay for it.
"They keep buying three- and six-month swaps," she said.
In the spot market, the dollar showed a bid tone amid ample money market liquidity and uncertainty over whether the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) would accept the election results.
PPP leaders were meeting on Thursday and said they would make a statement on Friday.
In Malaysia, the ringgit was sandwiched between offshore dollar demand around 2.5145 and local corporate dollar sales around 2.5190/2.5200.
Dealers said the market was awaiting the release of Malaysia's April money supply data.
A Reuters poll of 10 economists produced an average forecast of 20.4 percent broad money M3 growth and 20.2 percent M2 growth.

The Singapore dollar gained from continued liquidation of long ringgit/Sing positions, but its rise was blocked by U.S. dollar purchases by local banks, believed to be on behalf of the de facto central bank.
"If ringgit/Sing breaks below 0.5680 convincingly, we could see more liquidation," the U.S. bank dealer said, adding that the next support level would be at 0.5650.
"There are (U.S. dollar) bids around 1.4280/90. We could still go lower but we would probably need to see the G7 currencies lower first," he added.
The ringgit/Sing cross was quoted at 0.5676/82 at 0450 GMT whil dollar/Sing was at 1.4283/93.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
